problem_statement: The Codrops Developer/Designer Page Layout is a one-screen portfolio demo for Annie Fox with a designer/coder mode switch, menu links, a piece-based portrait effect using img/normal.jpg, img/alt.jpg and img/code.jpg, plus a Hired sponsor mark. Below the hero it exposes a compact local portfolio asset strip: four real bundled image cards (the portraits, the code texture and the sponsor mark). Three things are wrong or incomplete. (1) On a phone the local-asset card row is a fixed non-wrapping row that shoves the whole page off the right edge. (2) The site's asset 'lane' taxonomy (Portraits / Textures / Sponsor) is meant to appear as a shared 'Asset lanes' rail in the hero profile block, in the asset strip section AND in the footer, so the same rail vocabulary is met everywhere, but it is not consistently placed. (3) The asset strip has a filter (All assets / Portraits / Textures / Sponsor) that must update a 'Showing:' readout when a lane is selected. Repair the mobile overflow so the card row wraps, place the shared Asset lanes rail in all three sections in the dark Codrops palette, and wire the asset filter so clicking a lane updates the #asset-readout readout. Do not replace the animated pieces effect, change the Designer/Coder switch, or introduce unrelated or remote media.
required_content: Keep the existing Codrops portfolio page runnable as a static site with Annie Fox, On Interface Design, Portfolio, Case Studies, Musings, Designer, Coder, Work with me, the Coder-mode menu items, the piece-based portrait effect, the sponsor block, and the existing JS/CSS intact.

Keep the compact local asset strip with the exact text Local portfolio asset strip, Design portrait: img/normal.jpg, Alternate portrait: img/alt.jpg, Code texture: img/code.jpg, and Sponsor mark: sponsor/hired.png, using real local img elements for img/normal.jpg, img/alt.jpg, img/code.jpg and sponsor/hired.png with the exact alt text Annie Fox normal portrait asset, Annie Fox alternate portrait asset, Annie Fox code texture asset, and Hired sponsor mark asset.
Repair the local-asset card row so it wraps and stays readable without horizontal overflow on desktop, tablet and mobile while leaving the original title, menu, sponsor, and bottom controls visible.

Place the shared Asset lanes rail (class asset-rail with the section modifiers asset-rail--profile, asset-rail--library and asset-rail--footer, title Asset lanes, chips Portraits / Textures / Sponsor) in the hero profile block, in the asset strip section AND in the footer so the same rail is met on every part of the page, styled in the dark Codrops palette with mint accent, thin border and restrained chips.
Wire the asset filter so clicking All assets / Portraits / Textures / Sponsor marks the button active AND updates the #asset-readout terminal readout to Showing: <selected lane>.
Keep the Designer/Coder switch usable on desktop and mobile, including the code-mode menu items On Coding, Experiments, Current Projects, Tutorials, and > Find me on GitHub.

Build the strip from a shared local-asset card pattern with four real img cards and matching h3 captions; do not ship an off-system standalone cheatsheet, a filename list, or a page that is not registered in the shared navigation.
design_constraints: Preserve the one-screen Codrops concept: dark background, centered portrait pieces, mint designer accent, red coder accent, sparse top controls, right-aligned menu, bottom switch, and sponsor placement.
Do not replace the pieces effect with static img tags; the new images are explanatory asset evidence while the existing .pieces background images continue to drive the main visual effect.

Keep the change dependency-free and localized to index.html, the existing CSS files and js/asset-filter.js; do not add build tooling, external image services, routers, modals, carousels, or generated screenshots.

Use stable responsive CSS with a wrapping card row, bounded widths, fixed thumbnail heights and readable captions; the repaired card row must NOT rely on overflow-x:hidden to mask a still-wide row — the document itself must not overflow the viewport on mobile.
The Asset lanes rail must keep the reference dark Codrops palette (mint-tinted ground, thin mint border, small radius, outlined mint chips) — a collapsed off-palette dark slab is not faithful.
Do not rename Annie Fox, remove menu items, remove the sponsor block, delete the Designer/Coder switch, change image filenames, or hide the original Hired sponsor link.
state_constraints: desktop_initial, tablet_initial and mobile_initial protect the original one-screen portfolio composition (with the hero profile Asset lanes rail) before task-specific assertions.

desktop_asset_strip, tablet_asset_strip and mobile_asset_strip verify the local asset strip, captions, real image elements, the library Asset lanes rail, and the repaired responsive card row across viewport sizes.
desktop_footer_regression verifies the footer-section Asset lanes rail (the cross-section consistency invariant) and that the footer band renders.
desktop_coder_mode and mobile_coder_mode click the existing Coder switch and verify the original code-mode menu remains usable after the strip/rail are added.
desktop_asset_filter clicks the Portraits asset filter button and verifies the #asset-readout terminal readout updates to the selected lane (changed_from desktop_asset_strip).

change_completion: The page contains the required Local portfolio asset strip text and four exact asset captions with real local img elements and the required alt text.
The shared Asset lanes rail is present in the profile, asset-library and footer sections and the asset filter updates the #asset-readout readout on click.
design_consistency: The strip and the Asset lanes rail follow the original dark Codrops portfolio style with mint accent, thin borders and restrained scale.
The original pieces effect remains the primary visual surface instead of being replaced by a static gallery, and the rail keeps the mint palette rather than a collapsed dark slab.
responsive: Desktop and tablet layouts show the card row without horizontal overflow or collisions with the menu and switch.
Mobile layout wraps the card row so the document does not overflow the viewport while preserving the title, right menu, bottom Designer/Coder switch and sponsor visibility.
regression: Annie Fox, the design menu, Work with me, sponsor copy, and Designer/Coder controls remain present.
Coder mode still exposes On Coding, Experiments, Current Projects, Tutorials, and > Find me on GitHub.

metadata.design_goal: repair a real responsive/consistency/interaction regression on real repo content
metadata.source_repo_kind: Static Codrops portfolio layout concept with piece-based portrait assets, mode switch, sponsor image, menus, and no build step
metadata.selected_repo_reason: Runnable static portfolio whose bundled portrait/sponsor assets and designer/coder lane vocabulary make it a natural host for repairing a local-asset card-row mobile overflow, promoting a shared Asset lanes rail across sections, and wiring an asset filter readout.

author_notes: Slot slot_283 targets portfolio / regression_continuity / repair / component / L4 on the Codrops Developer/Designer Annie Fox layout. It repairs the local-asset card-row mobile overflow, promotes the Asset lanes rail across the profile, asset-library and footer sections, and wires the asset-filter readout while preserving the one-screen composition, the portrait imagery (img/normal.jpg, img/alt.jpg, img/code.jpg, sponsor/hired.png) and the Designer/Coder switch.
